title: Georgia fines 2 companies over data center, power plant permit violations
source_used: Atlanta News First; text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-17.txt
key_facts: The Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) fined two companies a combined $42,500 in Newton County for installing engines before getting construction permits.
VoltaGrid (power plant) pays $11,500 and Serverfarm (neighboring data center) pays $31,000, under consent orders.
EPD found eight VoltaGrid engines and 37 Serverfarm diesel emergency generators being installed, none connected to fuel or power.
VoltaGrid began installing around 29 May 2026 and Serverfarm on 9 Mar 2026; both blamed a misunderstanding.
Neither company admitted liability; the orders are not a finding of a violation of state law.
VoltaGrid agreed to keep construction stopped until it has a permit.
Advocate Maurice Carter of Sustainable Newton calls the fines small but a step toward accountability.
quote_evidence: Georgia regulators have fined two companies a combined $42,500 for installing engines at a data center and a neighboring power plant in Newton County before obtaining required construction permits, according to consent orders issued by the Georgia Environmental Protection Division.
Both orders state they do not constitute a finding or adjudication of a violation of state law, and neither company, by consenting to the orders, made any admission of liability.
Under its consent order, Serverfarm agreed to pay a civil penalty of $31,000 within 30 days of the order’s execution.
why_it_matters_hint: State fines are small, and the case shows local groups pushing for permit enforcement on data center projects.
event_date: consent orders reported 6 Oct 2026; violations found 29 Jun 2026
notes: Violations date from spring 2026; the new fact is the consent orders and fines.
